title: convergence_drainer's max_rounds cap is not forwarded to plan_convergence.evaluate_plan — kernel returns NEXT_ROUND_REQUIRED while drainer falls through to max_rounds verdict, leaving 0 plan_evaluated events and no verdict provenance
raised_by: ARIA-V10.5 endurance cycle 1 (cyc-2026-05-21 post-F-016..F-022 closure) — 3 P+C+CR rounds + 2 revisions completed, but kernel emitted 0 plan_evaluated events, plan stayed in CROSS_REVIEWED, terminal_state never derived

evidence.what_should_have_happened: Round 3 with 5 material risks AND round_n == max_rounds=3 → kernel evaluate_plan returns terminal_state=HUMAN_REQUIRED with reason_codes=[material_cross_review_risks_present, max_rounds_reached] → plan_evaluated event fires → drainer reads HUMAN_REQUIRED ∈ TERMINAL_STATES → _derive_arbiter_verdict returns 'scope_abort' → verdict_provenance appended → ConvergenceResult returned to cycle_runner → operator sees structured terminal state.
evidence.what_actually_happened: Drainer at round_n=3 (its max_rounds=3) called evaluate_plan(plan_id, round_number=3, base_dir) — WITHOUT max_rounds kwarg. Kernel defaulted to MAX_CROSS_REVIEW_ROUNDS=5. Kernel's _evaluate_cross_review_state saw round_number=3 < max_rounds=5 with blockers → returned terminal_state='NEXT_ROUND_REQUIRED' with event_appended=False. Drainer read terminal_state=None (next_round_required response shape has no 'state' key), persisted round=4, loop iteration ended (range(1, 4) exhausted), fell through to line 926, returned ConvergenceResult(arbiter_verdict='max_rounds') WITHOUT firing a kernel plan_evaluated event. cycle_runner observed the drainer verdict but the kernel ledger has zero terminal-state evidence, so verdict_provenance, implementation_requested, and operator-facing HUMAN_REQUIRED signals never emitted.

structural_root_cause.ssot_drift: convergence_drainer.run_convergence_drainer accepts max_rounds (default 4) and uses it to bound the round loop. plan_convergence.evaluate_plan accepts max_rounds (default MAX_CROSS_REVIEW_ROUNDS=5) and uses it to decide HUMAN_REQUIRED vs NEXT_ROUND_REQUIRED. These two caps are independent variables in the source — the drainer never tells the kernel WHICH cap is in effect for this cycle.
structural_root_cause.lesson: Two independent components reasoning about the same 'last round of the cycle' boundary will diverge unless one tells the other the canonical value. The kernel is the SSoT for terminal-state derivation (it owns the state machine + the plan_evaluated event + reason codes). The drainer is the SSoT for the operator-imposed cap (CLI flag, factory profile, runtime override). The two SSoTs must intersect at the evaluate_plan callsite — anything else is drift.
structural_root_cause.tier_1_anchor: Same root pattern as F-018/F-019/F-020 (SSoT drift across components) but at the runtime-parameter layer instead of the envelope-schema layer. F-021/F-022 closed the state-machine round-counter advancement; F-024 closes the kernel/drainer round-cap parameter parity. Together F-021 + F-022 + F-024 form the complete round-N → round-(N+1) → terminal-state transition contract.

tier_1_architectural_fix.scope: convergence_drainer's evaluate_plan call must forward the drainer's own max_rounds — kernel and drainer now share a single round-cap value per cycle.
files_changed: aria-kernel/tests/invariants/v10/test_phase_v10_5_phase_4_drainer_kernel_max_rounds_ssot.py (4 Tier-3 invariants — source presence, runtime parity, terminal-state derivation, verdict provenance)
tier_1_architectural_fix.tier_rationale: Tier-1 (make impossible): by passing the drainer's max_rounds into evaluate_plan, the kernel state machine can no longer disagree with the drainer about which round is the last — the kernel always uses the value the drainer actually capped on. The architectural truth ('the drainer's loop bound IS the kernel's terminal-state derivation bound') is now expressed structurally at the callsite, not implicitly via two separate defaults. Tier-3 (make detectable): 4 invariants catch any future regression where (a) the kwarg is dropped, (b) a hardcoded literal replaces max_rounds, (c) the runtime exhibits the pre-fix divergence, (d) the verdict_provenance event fails to fire on terminal cycles.

kernel_code_changes: 1-line keyword argument addition on convergence_drainer.py line 812-816 evaluate_plan call. plan_convergence.evaluate_plan unchanged (it already accepts max_rounds as a kwarg with MAX_CROSS_REVIEW_ROUNDS=5 default). v8 invariant suite (round-loop structure assertions) unaffected — the loop bound is still drainer's max_rounds; only the kernel-side reasoning is now aware of that same bound.

expected_impact_on_endurance.before_fix: Long cycles that exhaust the drainer's max_rounds with non-trivial blockers emit zero plan_evaluated events. Verdict-provenance ledger silent. Operator sees arbiter_verdict='max_rounds' from the drainer's fallthrough path but has no kernel evidence of WHY rounds blocked (reason_codes never appended to plan_evaluated event). implementation_requested never fires even on CONVERGED-eligible cycles that happened to land on round_n == max_rounds.
expected_impact_on_endurance.after_fix: Drainer's terminal round either CONVERGES (all gates pass → plan_evaluated event with CONVERGED → arbiter_verdict='converged' → implementation_requested fires) or HUMAN_REQUIRES (blockers present → plan_evaluated event with HUMAN_REQUIRED + reason_codes from _evaluate_cross_review_state's blockers list → arbiter_verdict mapped per _derive_arbiter_verdict table → verdict_provenance event appended). Operator now sees structured terminal evidence in the kernel ledger for every cycle that exhausts max_rounds.
